title: routerPlugin
summary: Configure flat route discovery and development server transport.

sections.title: Parameters
sections.body: directory defaults to src/routes. To use manual tables, provide both clientRoutes and serverRoutes paths relative to the Vite project.

sections.title: Returns
sections.body: A Vite plugin. fileRouter is an alias of routerPlugin.

sections.title: Usage
sections.body: Import this API from one of the entry points listed above. Keep server and build helpers in their dedicated subpaths.

sections.title: Behavior and edge cases
sections.body: Requires Vite 8 or newer. Import virtual:smolter/routes for the generated table. Server loader/action exports must be named re-exports from separate files. Export-star and inline server handlers, including destructured bindings and class declarations named loader/action, are rejected in browser route modules. Keep secrets and server initialization in the separate server module; route modules run in the browser. Development responses preserve separate cookies, including session deletion, and use the shared streaming response writer; production still needs a server adapter.

sections.title: Request body limit (0.5.2)
sections.body: Node createRequestHandler and Vite applicationPlugins/routerPlugin default to maxBodySize: 1048576 (1 MiB). Oversized declared lengths are rejected before reading; chunked bodies are counted as received and return 413 before application handlers run. The limit includes multipart overhead and counts received bytes, not decompressed content. Configure the same finite, nonnegative integer in production and development for intentionally larger uploads; zero permits only empty bodies. Keep hosting timeouts, rate/concurrency limits and any decompression limits. Low-level webRequest accepts this limit as its fourth argument and throws a Response for policy or size rejection; the provided middleware sends it automatically.

sections.title: Malformed development requests (0.5.2)
sections.body: The plugin guards Vite's Connect request entrypoint because URL parsing happens before middleware. Malformed targets receive a generic, non-cacheable 400 without terminating the server. The guard remains active after Vite restarts and in middleware mode; it is installed once per Connect instance. Unexpected failures still reach the hosting error callback or server logger. A parent host that parses requests before invoking Vite must handle its own parser errors. This does not modify standalone Vite or production hosting.

sections.title: Custom namespace
sections.body: namespace renames every client-visible Smolter identifier from one Vite option. It must start with a lowercase letter and contain at most 32 lowercase letters or digits, so derived HTML, header, URL and inline-script names stay valid. With namespace: "app", data requests use /path.__app, redirects use X-app-Redirect, the hydration script is #app-data, deferred data uses window.__appDeferred and __app* sentinels, streaming attributes are data-app-stream and data-app-preserve, recovery uses the app:deployment session key, and deploymentPlugin emits app-manifest.json. Vite compiles the value into browser and SSR bundles, including Smolter's own modules, so production browser output contains no smolter identifiers. Set it once on applicationPlugins or fileRouter; deploymentPlugin reads the same resolved value. A createRequestHandler imported outside the Vite build needs the same namespace option. Changing the namespace changes the wire format, so deploy browser and server builds together. Module ids such as virtual:smolter/routes stay build-time only and never reach the browser.
